the trade-offs to consider when implementing the required level of tenant isolation.
the design of cloud-based software systems and how to implement the appropriate degree of isolation between tenants to achieve the performance and resource requirements of the application.

the degree of tenant isolation is improved when careful consideration is made of all the factors identified in our explanatory framework.
the degree of tenant isolation is influenced by the trade-offs, the commonalities, the differences and the software process.
tenant isolation can be achieved in multi-tenancy, however, this comes with trade-offs and compromises.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
tenant isolation should be considered as a trade-off between performance and isolation.

tenant isolation is a complex problem, and the trade-offs, the commonalities, differences and the framework we present can help software designers and architects to understand the trade-offs to consider when achieving their degree of tenant requirements.

the degree of isolation between tenants is improved when careful consideration is paid to how to handle workload, locking of resources, and selection of multi-tenant pattern; and when the generated data is small, the cloud resource consumption is low, the software process is not sensitive to workload, the client latency and bandwidth are high, the software process does not generate many files, and customization and plug-ins are adopted.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is no single degree of tenant isolation that is best for all software services.
the degree of tenant isolation is affected by a number of factors.
the degree of isolation can be improved by careful consideration of the trade-offs, and commonalities, when designing multi-tenant cloud applications.
